title: Bounded gate scan step
statement: Let $\tau$ be a scan task, let $n$ be a natural number, let $w$ and $E$ be finite bit strings, and let $o$ assign a Boolean answer to each bit string at the sole oracle index. Suppose that for every natural number $q$, the oracle answer on the pairing of the unary string of length $n$ with the binary expansion of $q$ equals the bit of $E$ at position $q$, taking the answer to be false beyond the end of $E$. Let $B$ be a natural number with $|E|\le B$, let $g$ be a directed acyclic graph gate, and let $p,c,a$ be natural numbers such that the suffix of $E$ beginning at position $p$ is the concatenation of $1$, the encoding of $g$, and a remainder, with $c+1\le B$ and $a\le B$. Then there is a natural number $a'\le B$ such that the scan for task $\tau$, started in its gate-reading state with registers $(p,c,a)$ and no answer yet, reaches its next gate-reading state with registers $(p+1+|\mathrm{encode}(g)|,c+1,a')$ and no answer yet, with every register at most $B$ in each configuration strictly before arrival.
